title: Maintaining Proper Pipe Slope for Gravity Drainage
description: Maintaining correct pipe slope is critical for self-cleaning gravity drainage. If horizontal drainage pipes lack adequate pitch, solids settle out of the wastewater stream and form persistent blockages. Conversely, excessive slope can cause liquids to flow faster than solids, leaving heavy debris behind to accumulate. Standard practice requires a consistent slope—typically determined by pipe diameter and local plumbing code. Regular inspections help identify pipe sags or displaced pipe hangers that compromise proper drainage grade over time.

Maintaining Proper Pipe Slope for Gravity Drainage

Maintaining correct pipe slope is critical for self-cleaning gravity drainage. If horizontal drainage pipes lack adequate pitch, solids settle out of the wastewater stream and form persistent blockages. Conversely, excessive slope can cause liquids to flow faster than solids, leaving heavy debris behind to accumulate. Standard practice requires a consistent slope—typically determined by pipe diameter and local plumbing code. Regular inspections help identify pipe sags or displaced pipe hangers that compromise proper drainage grade over time.
